text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wednesday:

- Swiss annual inflation rate rose by 0.2 percentage point to 0.8 percent in October, the Federal Statistics Office reported. The average annual inflation rate for 1996 amad 1997 is expected to be around 1.0 percent.
- Swiss Social Democratic politician Werner Marti, who is a

cantonal minister, member of parliament and ombudsman for consumer prices at the same time, will resign from his post as member of the cantonal government in Glarus. Marti was citicized for accumulating too many jobs.
- Swiss machine tools manufacturer Mikron will axe 68 jobs.

- The largest Swiss brewery group, Feldschloesschen-Huerlimann, will shut three local breweries in Fribourg (Cardinal), Berne (Gurten), and Zurich (Huerlimann). Some 680 job will be cut. - More than 50 percent of the adult population does not use a condom when having sex with an unknown person, a report by a Swiss anti-AIDS organisation said.
- Around 10 farmers who took part in a demonstration last week in Berne and who sustained burns from tear gas are considering legal steps against the Bernese police.
